name: Second 2-3-74 (Metz, 1977)
date_basis: Metz speech text; Sutin biography; Exegesis post-Metz
summary: Around the time of his Metz, France speech in September 1977, PKD reports a partial recurrence of the 2-3-74 phenomenology — pink-light states, AI Voice activity, and the Black Iron Prison overlay returning at intervals.
description: PKD's September 1977 speech at the Metz international science fiction convention — published as 'If You Find This World Bad, You Should See Some of the Others' — was the public unveiling of his Phil-from-the-future hypothesis. Around the speech (before, during, and after), PKD reports a partial recurrence of the 2-3-74 phenomenology: pink-light states, AI Voice activity, and Black Iron Prison perceptions. He treats this as confirmation that 2-3-74 is not a single past event but a state that can recur.

pkd_interpretations.interpretation: The transmissions are from a future Phil Dick to me; the experience can recur because future-Phil is still transmitting.
VALIS is still active; the Metz event is a renewed transmission.

scholar_interpretations.interpretation: Sutin treats the Metz speech as the public moment at which PKD's mystical claims went on the record in Europe.
Davis frames Metz as the first European reception of PKD's California-visionary turn.

primary_sources.excerpt: *If You Find This World Bad, You Should See Some of the Others* (Metz, 1977).

primary_quote: We are living in a computer-programmed reality, and the only clue we have to it is when some variable is changed and some alteration in our reality occurs.
pkd_doubt_evidence: PKD wonders openly whether the Metz state was performance under public-speaking pressure.
